questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Detecting NaN and infinite gradients” in this lesson?
options: This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
Identify the value being differentiated and the scalar objective; compare the resulting gradient with a tiny analytical or numerical check.
This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
questions.answer_key: Identify the value being differentiated and the scalar objective; compare the resulting gradient with a tiny analytical or numerical check.
questions.explanation: Detecting NaN and infinite gradients: Identify the value being differentiated and the scalar objective; compare the resulting gradient with a tiny analytical or numerical check.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “In-place modification errors”, what should a learner verify?
options: Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
verify that the target tensor tracks gradients, the output is connected to it, and the gradient matches an analytical or finite-difference check.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
questions.answer_key: verify that the target tensor tracks gradients, the output is connected to it, and the gradient matches an analytical or finite-difference check.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: verify that the target tensor tracks gradients, the output is connected to it, and the gradient matches an analytical or finite-difference check.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Gradient checking”?
options: Gradients accumulate by default; reset them at the intended point and avoid unsafe in-place mutation of values needed by autograd.
Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
questions.answer_key: Gradients accumulate by default; reset them at the intended point and avoid unsafe in-place mutation of values needed by autograd.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Gradients accumulate by default; reset them at the intended point and avoid unsafe in-place mutation of values needed by autograd.
